sn46.11:1.1: “Bhikkhus, whatever living beings there are which assume the four postures—
sn46.11:1.2: sometimes walking, sometimes standing, sometimes sitting, sometimes lying down—all assume the four postures based upon the earth, established upon the earth.
sn46.11:1.3: So too, based upon virtue, established upon virtue, a bhikkhu develops and cultivates the seven factors of enlightenment.
sn46.11:2.2: Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops the enlightenment factor of mindfulness,
sn46.11:2.3: which is based upon seclusion, dispassion, and cessation, maturing in release…. He develops the enlightenment factor of equanimity, which is based upon seclusion, dispassion, and cessation, maturing in release.
sn46.11:2.4: It is in this way, bhikkhus, that a bhikkhu, based upon virtue, established upon virtue, develops and cultivates the seven factors of enlightenment.”
